heading: General Design Requirements — Vehicle Configuration
embed_text: T 2.1.3 General Design Requirements — Vehicle Configuration: Open wheel vehicles must satisfy the following, see also Figure 4: The wheel/tire assembly must be unobstructed when viewed from the side. No part of the vehicle may enter a keep-out-zone defined by two lines extending vertically from positions 75 mm in front of and 75 mm behind the outer diameter of the front and rear tires in the side view of the vehicle, with steering system straight ahead. This keep-out zone extends laterally outward from the inboard plane of the wheel/tire assembly indefinitely. The keep-out-zone at the rear tires extends up to 700 mm above the ground. An additional keep-out-zone extends from the top of the rear tire to 700 mm above the ground and 150 mm inboard from the inboard plane of the rear tire. It is bounded longitudinally by the 75 mm keep-out-zone of the rear tire. Figure 4: Keep-out-zones for the definition of an open-wheeled vehicle

embed_text: T 2.1.4 General Design Requirements — Vehicle Configuration: No part of the vehicle forward of the vertical plane through the leading edge of the front tires must enter the variable keep-out zone, see Figure 5. heading: General Chassis Design — Laminate Testing
embed_text: T 3.6.1 General Chassis Design — Laminate Testing: If composite materials are used for any part of the primary structure (except for the AIP) or the TSAC the team must: build a representative test panel which must measure exactly 275 mm × 500 mm that has the same design, laminate and fabrication method as used for the respective part of the primary structure represented as a flat panel. The sides of the test panel must not be laminated (core material must be visible). perform a 3-point bending test on this panel. The data from these tests and pictures of the test samples and test setup must be included in the SES. In the pictures, the following must be identifiable: distance between the two supports, dimensions of the load applicator and test sample marking as per T 3.6.6. The test results must be used to derive strength and stiffness properties used in the SES formula for all laminate panels. Representative test panels for parts of the TSAC may use smaller dimensions, provided that the panel core thickness is 5 mm or smaller. This representative test panel must then measure 150 mm × 275 mm. heading: General Chassis Design — Impact Attenuator (IA)
embed_text: T 3.17.7 General Chassis Design — Impact Attenuator (IA): A team may use one of the “standard” FSAE IAs without physical testing, provided that all of the following is fulfilled: A 1.5 mm solid steel AIP is used, that is welded along its full perimeter to a steel bulkhead or a 4 mm solid aluminium AIP is used, that is bolted to any bulkhead with a minimum of eight 8 mm metric grade 8.8 bolts. The adhesive used to mount the “standard” IA to the AIP has a shear strength of at least 24 MPa. T 3.19.4 is fulfilled regarding aerodynamic device and sensor positions relative to the AIP. If the front bulkhead has an overall width greater than 400 mm and/or an overall height greater than 350 mm, a diagonal or X-bracing that is a front bulkhead support tube or an approved equivalent per T 3.2, or equivalent for monocoque bulkheads, must be included. If the “standard” honeycomb IA is used, the IA must be of pre-crushed type. If one or more of the above conditions are not met, physical testing must be carried out to prove that the AIP does not permanently deflect more than 25 mm. heading: General Chassis Design — Impact Attenuator Test Requirements
embed_text: T 3.19.1 General Chassis Design — Impact Attenuator Test Requirements: The IA assembly, when mounted on the front of a vehicle with a total mass of 300 kg and impacting a solid, non-yielding impact barrier with a velocity of impact of 7 m/s, must meet the following requirements: Decelerate the vehicle at a rate not exceeding 20 g average and 40 g peak. The energy absorbed in this event must meet or exceed 7350 J. Teams using the standard IA are not required to submit test data with their IAD report, but all other requirements must be included. Equivalent (higher) test velocities are only allowed to accommodate for a lower total testing mass, as long as the energy absorbed is 7350 J or more. If these requirements cannot be met, a team must use the standard IA. Abbreviations: IA = Impact Attenuator; IAD = Impact Attenuator Data

heading: General Chassis Design — Impact Attenuator Test Requirements
embed_text: T 3.19.2 General Chassis Design — Impact Attenuator Test Requirements: During the IA test: The IA must be attached to the AIP using the intended vehicle attachment method. The IA assembly must be attached to a test fixture that has geometry representative of the intended primary structure and equal or higher stiffness and strength. When no baseline design for the AIP is used, see T 3.17.3, the test fixture must be a copy of the intended primary structure (i.e. materials, lay-up, joining methods). There must be at least 50 mm clearance rearwards of the AIP to the test fixture. No part of the AIP may permanently deflect more than 25 mm beyond the position of the AIP before the test. The representative test fixture of the intended primary structure may not be structurally compromised (i.e. no cracks) after the test. Abbreviations: AIP = Anti Intrusion Plate; IA = Impact Attenuator

heading: Driver Restraint System — Belts - General
embed_text: T 5.2.1 Driver Restraint System — Belts - General: All drivers must use a 6-point or 7-point restraint harness meeting the following specifications: All driver restraint systems must meet SFI Specification 16.1, SFI Specification 16.5, SFI Specification 16.6 or FIA specification 8853/2016. The belts must bear the appropriate dated labels. The material of all straps must be in perfect condition. There must be a single metal-to-metal latch type quick release for all straps. All lap belts must incorporate a tilt lock adjuster (“quick adjuster”). A tilt lock adjuster in each portion of the lap belt is highly recommended. Lap belts with “pull-up” adjusters are recommended over “pull-down” adjusters. Vehicles with a “reclined driving position” must have either anti-submarine belts with tilt lock adjusters (“quick adjusters”) or have two sets of anti-submarine belts installed. The shoulder harness must be the “over-the-shoulder type”. Only separate shoulder straps are allowed (i.e. “Y”-type shoulder straps are not allowed). The “H”-type configuration is allowed. The shoulder harness straps must be threaded through the three bar adjusters in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions. When a Frontal Head Restraint (FHR) device is used by the driver, minimum 50 mm wide shoulder harnesses are allowed. Abbreviations: FHR = Frontal Head Restraint

heading: Fasteners — Securing Fasteners
embed_text: T 10.2.2 Fasteners — Securing Fasteners: The following methods are accepted as positive locking mechanisms: Correctly installed safety wiring. Cotter pins. Nylon lock nuts (ISO 7040, ISO 10512, EN 1663 or an equivalent standard) for locations where no temperature rating above 80 °C is required. Prevailing torque lock nuts (DIN 980, ISO 7042 or an equivalent standard, and jet nuts or K-nuts). Locking plates. Tab washers. Any locking mechanism based on pre-tensioning or an adhesive is not considered a positive locking mechanism.

heading: Vehicle and Driver Equipment — Driver Equipment
embed_text: T 13.3.12 Vehicle and Driver Equipment — Driver Equipment: All driver equipment covered in T 13.3 must be in good condition. The officials reserve the right to impound all non-approved driver equipment until the end of the event.

heading: Internal Combustion Engine Powertrains — Engine Limitation

heading: Fuel and Fuel System — Fuel Injection System Requirements
embed_text: CV 2.5.2 Fuel and Fuel System — Fuel Injection System Requirements: The following requirements apply to HPI and DI fuel systems: All high pressure fuel lines must be stainless steel rigid line or Aeroquip FC807 smooth bore PTFE hose with stainless steel reinforcement and visible Nomex tracer yarn. Use of elastomeric seals is prohibited. Lines must be securely mounted every 100 mm by mechanical fasteners to structural engine components. The fuel rail must be securely mounted to the engine cylinder head with mechanical fasteners. The fastening method must be sufficient to hold the fuel rail in place with the maximum regulated pressure acting on the injector internals and neglecting any assistance from in-cylinder pressure acting on the injector tip. The threaded fasteners used to secure the fuel rail are considered critical fasteners and must comply with T 10. The fuel pump must be securely mounted to structural engine components. A fuel pressure regulator must be fitted between the high and low pressure sides of the fuel system in parallel with the DI boost pump. The external regulator must be used even if the DI boost pump comes equipped with an internal regulator. Before the Tilt Test specified in IN 7, engines fitted with mechanically actuated fuel pumps must be run to fill and pressure the system downstream of the high pressure pump. Abbreviations: DI = Direct Injection; HPI = High Pressure Injection

heading: Shutdown Circuit and Systems — Shutdown Circuit (SDC)
embed_text: EV 6.1.5 Shutdown Circuit and Systems — Shutdown Circuit (SDC): If the SDC is opened the TS must be shut down by opening all AIRs as well as the pre-charge relay and the voltage in the TS must drop to below 60 V DC and 50 V AC RMS in less than 5 s. The action of opening the AIRs may be delayed by ≤250 ms to signal the action to the motor controllers and reduce the TS current before the AIRs are opened. The AIR supply must be abruptly switched off before reaching the minimum AIR supply voltage. heading: General — Modifications and Repairs
embed_text: IN 1.5.1 General — Modifications and Repairs: After Technical Inspection, the only modifications allowed to the vehicle are: Adjustment of belts, chains and clutches Adjustment of the brake bias Adjustment of the driver restraint system, head restraint, seat and pedal assembly Substitution of the head restraint or seat insert for different drivers Adjustment to engine operating parameters, e.g. fuel mixture and ignition timing Adjustment of mirrors Adjustment of the suspension where no part substitution, other than springs, sway bars and shims, is required Adjustment of tire pressure Adjustment of winglet angles, but not the position of the complete aerodynamic device in relation to the vehicle Replenishment of fluids Replacement of defective tires or brake pads. Replacement tires and brake pads must be identical in material/composition/size to those presented and approved at Technical Inspection. Changing wheels and tires for “wet” or “damp” conditions as allowed in D 3.2 and D 7.6 Software calibration changes Recharging LV batteries Recharging TS accumulators (De-)Coupling of actuators and sensor repositioning as allowed in T 14.7 Installing and removing protective sensor covers, if approved during Technical Inspection Replacement of LV batteries. Replacement LV batteries must be identical and approved at Technical Inspection. Any other modification must be either approved by or performed under the supervision of Technical Inspection officials. Abbreviations: TS = Tractive System; LV = Low Voltage

heading: [EV ONLY] Electrical Inspection — Electrical Inspection General Definitions
embed_text: IN 4.1.1 [EV ONLY] Electrical Inspection — Electrical Inspection General Definitions: The insulation resistance between the TS and LVS ground is measured. Vehicles are probed with a test voltage based on their maximum TS voltage according to the following table: Maximum TS Voltage | Test Voltage ; ≤250 V | 250 V ; >250 V to ≤500 V | 500 V ; >500 V | 1000 V To pass this test, the measured insulation resistance must be at least 500 Ω/V related to the maximum TS voltage of the vehicle. Abbreviations: LVS = Low Voltage System; TS = Tractive System; EV = Electric Vehicle

heading: [EV ONLY] Electrical Inspection — Electrical Inspection General Definitions
embed_text: IN 4.1.2 [EV ONLY] Electrical Inspection — Electrical Inspection General Definitions: The IMD is tested by connecting a resistor between the TSMP, see EV 4.7 and LVS ground connector, see EV 4.7.8. The test is passed if the IMD shuts down the TS within 30 s at a fault resistance of 50 % below the response value which corresponds to 250 Ω/V. Abbreviations: LVS = Low Voltage System; TS = Tractive System; TSMP = Tractive System Measuring Point; EV = Electric Vehicle; IMD = Insulation Monitoring Device

heading: Skidpad — Skidpad Procedure
embed_text: D 4.2.1 Skidpad — Skidpad Procedure: A run consists of a sequence of laps in exactly the following order. The vehicle must enter perpendicular to the figure of eight and must take one full lap on the right circle to establish the turn. The next lap must be on the right circle and is timed. Immediately following the second lap, the vehicle must enter the left circle for the third lap. The fourth lap must be on the left circle and is timed. Immediately upon finishing the fourth lap, the vehicle must exit the track perpendicular to the figure of eight and moving in the same direction as entered.
